To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mTORC2 is necessary for the activation of the DNA damage checkpoint in response to the DNA damaging agent camptothecin.
mTORC2 inhibition by Torin2 promotes DNA damage-induced S-phase cell cycle arrest and that this effect requires Chk1 activation.

1) mTORC2 regulates Chk1 activity in the G2/M checkpoint, 2) the G2/M arrest induced by DNA damage requires mTORC 2-dependent activation of Chk1, 3) Chk1 phosphorylation at Ser317/345 is required for G2/M arrest and 4) Chk1 is phosphorylated at Ser345 by mTORC2
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mTORC2 in DNA damage response and repair, and the therapeutic potential of mTORC 2 inhibition in cancer treatment.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of DNA damage response (DDR) and cell cycle arrest.
the role of the mTORC2 complex in regulating the DNA damage response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TORC2 is a key player in the DNA-damage response.
mTORC2 is required for DNA-damage-induced S and G(2)/M arrest, and mTORC2 inhibition could enhance the efficacy of DNA-damaging agents.
TORC2 is not required for DNA-damaged induced cell cycle arrest in the S and G2 phases of the cell cycle, and that Chk1 is not a downstream target of mTORC2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TORC2 inhibition may be a promising therapeutic strategy for cancer patients, especially for patients who are treated with chemotherapy.
we show that mTORC2 is a critical regulator of the G2 checkpoint and that this regulation is independent of mTORC1.
TORC2 inhibition may enhance the efficacy of DNA-damaging chemotherapies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mTORC2 inhibition is a potential way to enhance the efficacy of chemotherapy in a variety of tumor types, including breast cancer, melanoma, glioblastoma, and lung cancer.
mTORC2 is required for DNA damage induced G2/M arrest.
mTORC2 inhibition can sensitize cancer cells to DNA damage induced by chemotherapy.
